title: Recursive Critique Layers: Measuring Error Accumulation Through Oversight Depth

original_idea.body:
# Recursive Critique Layers: Measuring Error Accumulation Through Oversight Depth

**Problem:** The recursive reward modeling literature (e.g., Leike et al. and 2026 survey discussions) argues oversight hierarchies stay aligned only if per-layer error is bounded, but there are few cheap empirical measurements of how errors compound as you stack oversight layers.

**Direction:** Build a stacked critique pipeline: answer -> critique -> critique-of-critique -> ... using open models, on a labeled QA task. Measure final verdict accuracy as a function of stack depth. Test whether each added layer corrects or amplifies the prior layer's errors, estimating an empirical per-layer error-propagation factor.

**Why it matters:** Recursive oversight is foundational but its empirical failure mode (compounding vs. self-correction) is under-measured. A depth-vs-accuracy curve directly addresses 'recursive protocols where each layer may have systematic errors.' Inference-only.

**Relevant context:** Scalable agent alignment via reward modeling (arXiv:1811.07871) and AI Alignment: A Comprehensive Survey (arXiv:2310.19852): recursive reward modeling stays aligned only if error accumulation is bounded across the hierarchy of overseers.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: empirically measuring whether stacked oversight layers compound or self-correct directly addresses a foundational recursive-oversight assumption.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Accessible: stacked critique pipeline with open models, measure accuracy vs depth; inference-only.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: depth-vs-accuracy curve + per-layer propagation factor; clear deliverable.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly foundational measurement on public models; weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Recursive reward modeling is old but a cheap empirical depth-vs-error measurement appears largely unmeasured.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Theory established but cheap empirical depth-vs-error curves appear largely unmeasured.
